title_en: Lanzhou Shenjun Logistics Co., Ltd. v. Lanzhou Minbai (Group) Co., Ltd. — dispute over tort
ruling_gist_en: 1. After a shareholders' general meeting of a joint stock company adopts a resolution, the validity of the resolution is not affected by whether the shareholders approve of it, before it is confirmed invalid. Whether the content of the shareholders' general meeting resolution has been actually performed does not affect its validity.

full_text_en:
Lanzhou Shenjun Logistics Co., Ltd. v. Lanzhou Minbai (Group) Co., Ltd. — dispute over tort

【Ruling Summary】

1. After a shareholders' meeting of a joint stock company adopts a resolution, the validity of the resolution is not affected by whether shareholders acknowledge it, until the resolution is confirmed invalid. Whether the content of the shareholders' meeting resolution has been actually implemented does not affect the validity of the resolution.

2. The capital surplus increased by a company due to acceptance of a gift belongs to the company and is the company's asset. A shareholder cannot claim that the portion of such capital surplus corresponding to its shareholding ratio belongs to itself. In the share-trading reform of a listed company, where the company's shareholders' meeting resolves to convert capital surplus into newly issued shares to be transferred to tradable shareholders, the tradable shareholders of the company may obtain the corresponding new shares in proportion to their shareholdings, whereas non-tradable shareholders cannot request the company to pay the corresponding new shares based on their shareholding ratios. Even if the shareholders' meeting resolution is invalid, the legal effect is only that the tradable shareholders cannot obtain the new shares; the non-tradable shareholders still cannot obtain such new shares.

3. In the share-trading reform of a listed company, the conversion of capital surplus into increased capital to be distributed to tradable shareholders does not result in a reduction of the company's assets. A claim by non-tradable shareholders that they should receive compensation for the corresponding portion of the alleged reduction in assets on the ground of asset diminution shall not be upheld.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2009) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 75

Appellant (Original Plaintiff): Lanzhou Shenjun Logistics Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 199 Yanning Road, Chengguan District, Lanzhou City, Gansu Province.

Legal Representative: Li Junfei, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Zhao Jinyuan, lawyer of Gansu Changtai Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhao Yihan, lawyer of Gansu Changtai Law Firm.

Respondent (Original Defendant): Lanzhou Minbai (Group) Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 120 Zhongshan Road, Lanzhou City, Gansu Province.

Legal Representative: Du Yongzhong, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Wang Dong, lawyer of Gansu Zhongtian Law Firm.

The Appellant Lanzhou Shenjun Logistics Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shenjun Company), in a dispute over tort with the Respondent Lanzhou Minbai (Group) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Minbai Company), appealed against the Civil Judgment (2008) Gan Min Er Chu Zi No. 10 rendered by the Gansu High People's Court to this Court. This Court formed a collegiate panel in accordance with the law, with Judge Wang Dongmin serving as Presiding Judge, and Acting Judges Lei Jiping and Li Jingping as members, to hear the case. The clerk Bai Xue served as the recorder. The case is now concluded.

The facts found by the original trial court are as follows: On April 21, 2006, the Sixteenth Meeting of the Fourth Board of Directors of Minbai Company considered and adopted the Company's "Share-Trading Reform Plan," the main contents of which were: 1. The largest non-tradable shareholder of Minbai Company, Honglou Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Honglou Group), would inject into the company without consideration a 36.6045% equity interest in Lanzhou Honglou Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. According to the "Audit Report" issued by Zhejiang Dongfang Zhonghui Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd., as of December 31, 2005, the audited book value of this portion of the equity interest was RMB 30,000,000. 2. To enable the 36.6045% equity interest in Lanzhou Honglou Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. injected by Honglou Group to be solely enjoyed by the tradable shareholders, Minbai Company would implement a targeted conversion of capital surplus to be distributed to tradable shareholders, amounting to 28,379,137 shares, equivalent to a targeted conversion of 2.1621 shares for every 10 tradable shares held. 3. Non-tradable shareholders other than Honglou Group would pay 9,589,497 shares to tradable shareholders. 4. The overall consideration level of the above combined plan was equivalent to every 10 tradable shares obtaining 2.89271 shares. On May 29, 2006, Minbai Company convened a shareholders' meeting, which considered and adopted the said "Share-Trading Reform Plan," and on June 2, 2006, published an announcement on the implementation of the share-trading reform plan. Because non-tradable shareholders including Shenjun Company (then named Lanzhou Shenjun Pharmaceutical Technology Co., Ltd., renamed to its current name Lanzhou Shenjun Logistics Co., Ltd. on October 20, 2008; hereinafter referred to as Shenjun Company) did not clearly indicate their consent to participate in this share-trading reform, the largest shareholder of Minbai Company, Honglou Group, advanced payment on their behalf of 3,119,196 shares, and the second largest shareholder, Lanzhou Minbai Foci Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Minfo Company), advanced payment on their behalf of 542,421 shares, totaling 3,661,617 shares advanced on behalf of non-tradable shareholders including Shenjun Company. After the First Extraordinary Shareholders' Meeting of Minbai Company in 2006 and the relevant shareholders' meeting concerning the share-trading reform adopted the share-trading reform plan, Shenjun Company filed a lawsuit with the Lanzhou Intermediate People's Court within the statutory period, requesting confirmation that the resolution of the extraordinary shareholders' meeting on May 29, concerning Honglou Group's purported gratuitous donation of equity assets which was in fact a non-public issuance of 28,379,138 new shares, was illegal, and requesting a judgment that the resolution of that shareholders' meeting to issue new shares by pricing the RMB 30,000,000 equity assets was invalid, among other things. The Lanzhou Intermediate People's Court, by Civil Judgment (2006) Lan Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 82, dismissed Shenjun Company's claims. Shenjun Company appealed against this judgment to the Gansu High People's Court. During the hearing, with the mediation of the Gansu High People's Court, Shenjun Company and Minbai Company reached a mediation settlement. The content of this mediation document (hereinafter referred to as Mediation Document No. 159) is as follows: Shenjun Company and Minbai Company jointly confirmed that the RMB 30,000,000 equity assets gratuitously donated by Honglou Group to Minbai Company were genuine and lawful. On this premise, the resolution adopted at the shareholders' meeting of Minbai Company on May 29, 2006, was lawful and valid, and there was no issue of infringement of Shenjun Company's lawful rights and interests; Shenjun Company abandoned all its claims; Minbai Company would continue to respect Shenjun Company's various rights and interests as a shareholder in the future, etc.

On June 6, 2007, Shenjun Company filed a lawsuit with the Gansu High People's Court, requesting that Minbai Company, Minfo Company, and Honglou Group, in accordance with Minbai Company's share-trading reform plan, immediately arrange for Shenjun Company to repay the consideration advanced on its behalf to Minfo Company and Honglou Group, together with interest, handle the procedures for the listing and trading of the shares of Minbai Company held by Shenjun Company, and remove the impediments to trading. During the trial of this case, with the mediation of the Gansu High People's Court, the parties reached a mediation settlement on June 29, 2007. This mediation document (hereinafter referred to as Mediation Document No. 24) recorded that Shenjun Company had repaid to Minfo Company and Honglou Group the shares advanced on its behalf, amounting to 1,621,479 shares, and Minbai Company arranged for the restricted tradable shares of Minbai Company held by Shenjun Company to be listed and traded.

Shenjun Company believed that it had repaid the consideration advanced by the first and second shareholders of Minbai Company, namely Honglou Group and Minfo Company. Of the 28,379,137 shares of Minbai Company converted from the RMB 30,000,000 equity assets genuinely and lawfully donated by Honglou Group without consideration, because Shenjun Company's shareholding ratio in Minbai Company at the time was 6.18%, Shenjun Company should be entitled to 1,753,800 shares on a pro rata basis. Therefore, Shenjun Company filed the instant lawsuit with the original trial court, requesting Minbai Company to compensate it for 1,753,800 shares, converted into monetary compensation of RMB 20,081,010 (calculated based on the average stock price of RMB 10 per share for the twenty trading days after the lifting of the lock-up and listing of the non-tradable shares of Minbai Company held by Shenjun Company) and corresponding interest, and that Minbai Company bear the case acceptance fees.

The original trial court additionally found that as of May 29, 2006, the total share capital of Minbai Company was 234,397,120 shares, and Shenjun Company held a total of 6,370,800 shares of Minbai Company.

After trial, the original trial court held: The basis for Shenjun Company's lawsuit was that, according to Minbai Company's share-trading reform plan, the company's largest shareholder, Honglou Group, had injected without consideration a 36.6045% equity interest in Lanzhou Honglou Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. into Minbai Company, and the 28,379,137 shares converted from the capital surplus formed by this donated asset should correspondingly be enjoyed by all non-tradable shareholders of Minbai Company, including Shenjun Company. However, the share-trading reform plan of targeting the conversion of this capital surplus to be distributed to all tradable shareholders was adopted by resolution of Minbai Company's shareholders' meeting. In accordance with the principle of capital majority rule and corporate autonomy, this resolution was lawful and valid, and was binding on Shenjun Company. Minbai Company's targeted distribution of all 28,379,137 shares to all tradable shareholders was carried out in accordance with the plan adopted by the shareholders' meeting resolution, and did not constitute an infringement of Shenjun Company's rights. Moreover, Shenjun Company had previously filed a lawsuit concerning the validity of that shareholders' meeting resolution, which was concluded by mediation. Shenjun Company's further lawsuit regarding the distribution of shares converted from capital surplus violated the principle of res judicata. There was also no contractual relationship between Shenjun Company and Minbai Company. Therefore, Shenjun Company's claims had no factual or legal basis, and this court did not support them. In summary, the original trial court, in accordance with Article 99 of the Company Law of the PRC, rendered the judgment: Dismissing Shenjun Company's claims. The case acceptance fee of RMB 154,172 was to be borne by Shenjun Company.

During the second instance of this Court, the original trial court issued Civil Ruling (2008) Gan Min Er Chu Zi No. 10, correcting clerical errors in the original judgment. The correction changed the phrase in the original judgment "Because Shenjun Pharmaceutical Company did not clearly indicate its consent to participate in this share-trading reform, the largest shareholder of Minbai Company, Honglou Group, advanced 3,119,196 shares on its behalf, and the second largest shareholder, Lanzhou Minbai Foci Group Co., Ltd., advanced 542,421 shares on its behalf, totaling 3,661,617 shares advanced on behalf of Shenjun Pharmaceutical Company" to "Because non-tradable shareholders including Shenjun Pharmaceutical Company did not clearly indicate their consent to participate in this share-trading reform, the largest shareholder of Minbai Company, Honglou Group, advanced 3,119,196 shares on their behalf, and the second largest shareholder, Lanzhou Minbai Foci Group Co., Ltd., advanced 542,421 shares on their behalf, totaling 3,661,617 shares advanced on behalf of non-tradable shareholders including Shenjun Pharmaceutical Company"; and changed the phrase "Shenjun Pharmaceutical Company repaid to Minfo Company and Honglou Group the shares advanced on its behalf, amounting to 3,661,617 shares" to "Shenjun Pharmaceutical Company repaid to Minfo Company and Honglou Group the shares advanced on its behalf, amounting to 1,621,479 shares."

Shenjun Company, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the original trial court, appealed to this Court, requesting that the original trial judgment be set aside, and that Minbai Company compensate Shenjun Company for 1,753,800 shares converted into monetary compensation of RMB 20,081,010 (calculated based on the average stock price of the non-tradable shares of Minbai Company held by Shenjun Company for the twenty trading days after the lifting of the lock-up and listing) and corresponding interest, and that Minbai Company bear the litigation costs of the first and second instances. The main reasons were:

1. The original trial judgment did not confirm the fact jointly confirmed by Shenjun Company and Minbai Company in Mediation Document No. 159 that the RMB 30,000,000 equity assets gratuitously donated by the largest shareholder of Minbai Company, Honglou Group, to Minbai Company were genuine and lawful. At the same time, the original trial judgment did not determine the crucial issue of whether the RMB 30,000,000 equity assets becoming the 28,379,137 newly increased shares of Minbai Company constituted a gratuitous donation and conversion or a non-public issuance of new shares.

2. A shareholders' meeting resolution must not violate laws and administrative regulations to be valid. The shareholders' meeting resolution involved in this case could only be lawful and valid if the gratuitous donation of the RMB 30,000,000 equity assets was genuine and lawful. If, after the RMB 30,000,000 equity assets gratuitously donated by Honglou Group to Minbai Company were converted into 28,379,137 new shares, they were still owned by Honglou Group, this would contradict the premise of a gratuitous donation. According to Mediation Document No. 159, the shareholders' meeting resolution should be unlawful and invalid. Moreover, the injection of RMB 30,000,000 assets by Honglou Group into Minbai Company becoming 28,379,137 new shares belonging to Honglou Group constituted a non-public issuance of new shares as defined in Article 10 of the Securities Law. This non-public issuance of new shares was not approved by the China Securities Regulatory Commission, violating the provisions of Article 13(2) of the Securities Law. Therefore, the content of the shareholders' meeting resolution regarding the conversion of the RMB 30,000,000 assets into 28,379,137 new shares of Honglou Group should be invalid.

3. The lawsuit to which Mediation Document No. 159 pertained was filed by Shenjun Company on the ground that the gratuitous donation of the RMB 30,000,000 equity assets by Honglou Group was false. That lawsuit was ultimately concluded by mediation on the basis that Shenjun Company and Minbai Company jointly confirmed that the gratuitous donation was genuine. However, the current case is one in which Shenjun Company claims that Minbai Company unlawfully disposed of Shenjun Company's lawful property obtained through accepting a gratuitous donation, thus seeking compensation from Minbai Company. This is a different lawsuit from the one settled by Mediation Document No. 159. The original trial judgment's dismissal of Shenjun Company's lawsuit on the ground of res judicata has no factual basis. Furthermore, Minbai Company gave away 1,753,800 newly increased shares of Minbai Company belonging to Shenjun Company as a result of accepting the gratuitous donation to Honglou Group. Minbai Company should bear liability for compensation (including corresponding interest). Shenjun Company's claim for compensation in the original trial was well-founded and should be supported. This case is a tort action. The original trial judgment's use of the absence of a contractual relationship between Shenjun Company and Minbai Company as one of the grounds for dismissing Shenjun Company's lawsuit has no factual or legal basis.

4. Shenjun Company did not object to the Minbai Company shareholders' meeting resolution's decision to donate 28,379,137 shares to all tradable shareholders as consideration. Shenjun Company believes that this consideration was paid by all non-tradable shareholders, not solely by Honglou Group. On the premise that the gratuitous donation was genuine and lawful, the shareholders' meeting resolution's action of giving the 28,379,137 shares belonging to all shareholders to Honglou Group as its consideration paid to all tradable shareholders constitutes Honglou Group's manipulation of the shareholders' meeting to misappropriate the property of the listed company, which is a criminal offense and should be transferred to the public security authorities. Moreover, the misappropriation of Minbai Company's property is a public prosecution case and is not subject to mediation.

5. According to the accounting standards promulgated by the Ministry of Finance, the surplus reserve formed by a company's acceptance of non-cash donations cannot be converted into share capital. In fact, the surplus reserve formed by the RMB 30,000,000 equity assets accepted by Minbai Company is still on the books. The surplus reserve of RMB 30,000,000 that the share-trading reform decided to convert was the surplus reserve that Minbai Company had accumulated over the years, and it had nothing to do with the RMB 30,000,000 donated equity assets. This also proves that the converted RMB 30,000,000 surplus reserve belonged to all tradable shareholders, and the 28,379,137 new shares converted from the surplus reserve were consideration paid by all non-tradable shareholders to all tradable shareholders, not consideration paid solely by Honglou Group to all tradable shareholders. According to the principle of same shares, same rights, Shenjun Company, as a non-tradable shareholder, should be entitled to 17,538,000 shares out of these 28,379,137 shares.

Minbai Company argued in its defense: Shenjun Company's appeal claims have no factual or legal basis and should be dismissed. The reasons are:

1. According to the principle of res judicata, the original trial court should not have accepted this case. Before filing the instant lawsuit in the original trial, Shenjun Company had already filed two lawsuits in court concerning the legality of the share-trading reform and the method of paying the share-trading reform consideration. Both cases were concluded by mediation, and the substantive content of the mediations was that Shenjun Company lost and withdrew its claims. Among them, Mediation Document No. 159 of the Gansu High People's Court stipulated: Shenjun Company and Minbai Company jointly confirmed that the donation of RMB 30,000,000 assets by Honglou Group was genuine and lawful. On this premise, the shareholders' meeting resolution of Minbai Company on May 29, 2006, was lawful and valid, and there was no issue of infringement of Shenjun Company's lawful rights and interests. Mediation Document No. 24 of the Gansu High People's Court stipulated that after the mediation agreement was performed, all rights and obligations between Shenjun Company and Minbai Company concerning the repayment of the consideration advanced for the share-trading reform would be terminated. Now, both mediation documents have been fully performed, and the rights and obligations between Shenjun Company and Minbai Company have been terminated. Shenjun Company made final dispositions of its rights and obligations in the share-trading reform process in the two aforementioned mediation documents. However, in this case, Shenjun Company again requested a judgment ordering Minbai Company to distribute to Shenjun Company the capital surplus formed by the assets gratuitously donated by Honglou Group to Minbai Company in exchange for the consideration shares paid to tradable shareholders during the share-trading reform. This constitutes a renewed lawsuit on the repayment of consideration advanced for the share-trading reform, which violates the principle of res judicata. In its appeal brief, Shenjun Company argued that this case is premised on the truth of the gratuitous donation, and further alleged that Minbai Company unlawfully disposed of Shenjun Company's lawful property obtained through the gratuitous donation, thus seeking compensation from Minbai Company. This, Shenjun Company claims, is a different legal relationship from the previous mediations. Minbai Company believes that the increase in capital surplus formed during the share-trading reform was precisely the result of Minbai Company's acceptance of the gratuitous donation of assets by its controlling shareholder, which constituted the consideration paid by all non-tradable shareholders for the share-trading reform. The donated assets, the book capital surplus formed, and the shares converted and distributed to tradable shareholders were all formed for the purpose of paying the share-trading reform consideration. They represent the same property interest in different forms at different stages of the share-trading reform. After repaying the advanced consideration with shares, Shenjun Company now seeks to retrieve the already-repaid consideration by claiming the surplus reserve should be distributed according to shareholding ratio. This is essentially a request to repay the consideration it advanced in the share-trading reform. Shenjun Company, in Mediation Document No. 159 and Mediation Document No. 24, confirmed the legality and validity of Minbai Company's share-trading reform plan and explicitly stated that the plan did not infringe upon Shenjun Company's lawful rights and interests, and also made dispositions of all rights and obligations concerning the repayment of the consideration advanced for the share-trading reform. Shenjun Company has no right to continue litigating, nor to assert any rights over the donated assets, the book capital surplus, or the shares converted and distributed to tradable shareholders.

II. Shenjun Company's claims have no basis, and from the nature of the creditor's rights, its claims cannot form any lawful creditor's rights.

1. Shenjun Company's claims lack a legal basis and do not constitute a debt arising from infringement. Shenjun Company asserts that Minbai Company received a gratuitous donation of RMB 30 million in assets from its controlling shareholder, which was converted into capital reserves. Based on the principle of equal rights for the same class of shares, Shenjun Company, as a shareholder, should be entitled to a proportionate share. Shenjun Company is mistaken in two aspects: First, "the same class of shares" under the principle of equal rights for the same class of shares does not mean that all shareholders hold identical rights regardless of the nature of their equity interests simply by holding shares in a company. Shenjun Company is a holder of non-tradable shares, and the content of its shareholder rights is fundamentally different from that of holders of tradable shares. The spirit of the China Securities Regulatory Commission's "Measures for the Administration of the Share-trading Reform of Listed Companies" is that holders of non-tradable shares must pay consideration to obtain tradability. It is precisely in accordance with this spirit that Honglou Group made a gratuitous donation of assets to Minbai Company, and then the company used capital reserves to make a targeted increase to the holders of tradable shares. Shenjun Company's claim to the right to distribute capital reserves based on the principle of equal rights for the same class of shares essentially seeks to obtain tradability without paying any consideration. Shenjun Company is demanding "the same rights" despite holding "a different class of shares." Second, the Company Law of the PRC does not provide that capital reserves shall be shared by all shareholders in proportion to their shareholdings. The revised Company Law of 2005 deleted the provision that "where a joint stock limited company converts its reserves into capital by a resolution of the shareholders' general meeting, it shall distribute new shares or increase the par value of each share in proportion to the original shareholdings of the shareholders," thereby establishing the legality of the method of targeted conversion of capital reserves. Shenjun Company's demand that "capital reserves shall be shared in proportion to shareholdings" has no basis. Third, the process and plan of Minbai Company's share-trading reform were approved by the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of Gansu Province and the Shanghai Stock Exchange, and were passed by the relevant shareholders' meeting with a 92.49% approval vote. In the two cases involving Mediation Document No. 159 and Mediation Document No. 24, the Gansu Higher People's Court also concluded the mediation on the basis of confirming the legality and validity of Minbai Company's share-trading reform plan. Shenjun Company itself acknowledges in its litigation documents that Honglou Group's gratuitous injection of equity assets into Minbai Company became capital reserves of Minbai Company, and was converted into shares for specific targets (i.e., all holders of tradable shares) through a resolution of the shareholders' general meeting, and that the procedures and content had no legal issues and were not illegal. It is evident that the process and plan of Minbai Company's share-trading reform were entirely legal and valid. Since there was no illegal act, there is no infringement. Therefore, Shenjun Company's infringement suit has no basis.

2. Shenjun Company's claims have no contractual basis and do not constitute a debt arising from contract. According to Mediation Document No. 24, Shenjun Company and the controlling shareholder of Minbai Company entered into a "Share Transfer Agreement." This agreement is the only agreement between the parties concerning the repayment of consideration advanced for the share-trading reform. This agreement does not contain any provision requiring Minbai Company to return capital reserves to Shenjun Company, nor is there any other agreement between the parties. Therefore, Shenjun Company's claims have no contractual basis and do not constitute a debt arising from contract.

III. There are errors in Shenjun Company's appeal brief.

1. In its appeal brief, Shenjun Company claims that the RMB 30 million in equity assets became 28,379,137 new shares belonging to the largest shareholder, and that according to Article 10 of the Securities Law, this constitutes a non-public issuance of new shares. Consequently, the resolution of the shareholders' general meeting regarding this part is invalid because the non-public issuance of new shares was not approved by the China Securities Regulatory Commission, in violation of Article 13 of the Securities Law. This understanding of Shenjun Company is erroneous. First, a targeted conversion of capital reserves is different from a new share issuance. Although a capital reserve conversion to share capital also increases the company's share capital, it is not a securities issuance activity. The fundamental characteristics of a securities issuance are the raising of funds and the offering of securities. Minbai Company's share-trading reform neither offered shares to the public nor raised funds. Moreover, the number of shares held by the controlling shareholder did not change before or after the reform, and it cannot be said that new shares were issued to the largest shareholder. Second, targeted conversion of capital reserves has become a mainstream method of consideration in the share-trading reform of listed companies. Nearly one hundred listed companies have undergone reform through this method, and hundreds of companies distribute year-end dividends through this method each year. Precisely because it is not a securities issuance activity, it does not require review by the China Securities Regulatory Commission and only needs to be passed by the shareholders' general meeting.

2. In its appeal brief, Shenjun Company claims that the largest shareholder manipulated the shareholders' general meeting to embezzle the company's property in a substantial amount. This is inconsistent with the facts. First, at the shareholders' general meeting held on May 29, 2006, due to the involvement of related-party transactions, the largest shareholder did not participate in the voting. Even so, the shareholders' general meeting still passed the share-trading reform plan with a 92.49% approval vote. Second, before and after the reform, the number of shares held by the largest shareholder of Minbai Company, Honglou Group, did not increase, nor did its assets or cash increase. Furthermore, Honglou Group donated RMB 30 million in equity assets to Minbai Company. It did not embezzle Minbai Company's property. On the contrary, the number of shares held by holders of tradable shares increased by 28,379,137 shares. If Shenjun Company believes that someone benefited from the embezzlement of assets, it should sue all holders of tradable shares, or directly apply for administrative reconsideration of the abstract administrative act of the "Measures for the Administration of the Share-trading Reform of Listed Companies." The issue of criminal liability raised by Shenjun Company in its appeal brief is irrelevant to this case.

In summary, Minbai Company believes that if Shenjun Company's claims were upheld, it would cause Shenjun Company's claims to violate the fundamental principle of majority rule by capital. Shenjun Company would then obtain tradability without paying any consideration, thereby violating the "Measures for the Administration of the Share-trading Reform of Listed Companies." The share-trading reforms of hundreds of listed companies that have already been completed using targeted conversion as a method of consideration would have to be redone, causing chaos in the securities market.

In addition to confirming the facts found by the court of first instance, this Court further finds the following:

1. The "Announcement on the Implementation Plan for the Share-trading Reform" of Minbai Company submitted by Shenjun Company in the first instance of this case states: The shareholders' general meeting of Minbai Company held on May 29, 2006, passed a resolution approving the company's "Share-trading Reform Plan," wherein 92.49% of the voting rights held by all shareholders participating in the meeting approved the resolution, and 91.13% of the voting rights held by all holders of tradable shares participating in the meeting approved the resolution. Shenjun Company acknowledged the authenticity of this resolution during cross-examination in the second instance of this Court.

2. The "Capital Verification Report" on Minbai Company prepared by Zhejiang Dongfang Zhonghui Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd. on July 6, 2006, submitted by Shenjun Company in the second instance, includes in Appendix 2 "Capital Verification Instructions" the following: The 36.6045% equity interest in Lanzhou Honglou Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. gratuitously injected by Honglou Group into Minbai Company was registered for change with the Lanzhou Administration for Industry and Commerce on May 30, 2006. The 28,379,137 shares targeted for conversion and issuance by Minbai Company to holders of tradable shares, as well as the 9,589,497 shares paid by non-tradable shareholders other than Honglou Group to holders of tradable shares, were directly credited to the securities accounts of the shareholders by China Securities Depository and Clearing Corporation Limited on June 6, 2006. The share premium under capital reserves on Minbai Company's books at the end of 2005 was RMB 95,142,730.69, of which RMB 28,379,137 was used for this share conversion, leaving a capital reserve - share premium balance of RMB 66,763,593.69.

This Court holds: After the shareholders' general meeting of Minbai Company passed a resolution adopting the "Share-trading Reform Plan," the validity of the plan is not affected by whether Shenjun Company acknowledges it. The "Share-trading Reform Plan" of Minbai Company stipulated that the 36.6045% equity interest in Honglou Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. injected by Honglou Group into Minbai Company (the audited book value of this equity asset was RMB 30 million) would be used by Minbai Company to implement a capital reserve conversion of 28,379,137 shares for its holders of tradable shares, and that non-tradable shareholders other than Honglou Group would pay a total of 9,589,497 shares to holders of tradable shares. This indicates that the RMB 30 million assets injected by Honglou Group into Minbai Company were consideration paid by Honglou Group to the holders of tradable shares for obtaining tradability for the shares it held in Minbai Company, not consideration paid by all non-tradable shareholders of Minbai Company to the holders of tradable shares. Shenjun Company's assertion that the 28,379,137 new shares converted by Minbai Company should be treated as consideration paid by all non-tradable shareholders to all holders of tradable shares, rather than merely consideration paid by Honglou Group to holders of tradable shares, lacks factual basis, and this Court does not support it.

The "Share-trading Reform Plan" of Minbai Company provided that, to ensure that the RMB 30 million equity assets injected by Honglou Group into Minbai Company were entirely enjoyed by the holders of tradable shares, Minbai Company would implement a targeted capital reserve conversion of 28,379,137 shares for its holders of tradable shares. This indicates that Honglou Group injected the RMB 30 million equity assets into Minbai Company for the purpose of allowing the holders of tradable shares to benefit from those assets. At the time the "Share-trading Reform Plan" was passed, Shenjun Company was a non-tradable shareholder of Minbai Company and should not enjoy the shares formed by the conversion of those assets. Shenjun Company's claim that it should be entitled to 1,753,800 shares from the targeted conversion, in proportion, like other holders of tradable shares, in accordance with the principle of equal rights for the same class of shares, is inconsistent with the provisions of the plan mentioned above because the "Share-trading Reform Plan" adopted by the resolution of Minbai Company's shareholders' general meeting explicitly provided that the targeted conversion shares were to be enjoyed by the holders of tradable shares of Minbai Company. Accordingly, this Court does not accept Shenjun Company's claim. This Court supports Minbai Company's submission that Shenjun Company cannot assert rights over the shares formed after Minbai Company's conversion. The "Capital Verification Instructions" submitted by Shenjun Company state that the 28,379,137 new shares after Minbai Company's targeted conversion were credited to the securities accounts of Minbai Company's holders of tradable shares on June 6, 2006. Therefore, Shenjun Company's assertion that these 28,379,137 new shares still belonged to Honglou Group is inconsistent with the facts, and this Court does not credit it.

The "Share-trading Reform Plan" of Minbai Company explicitly provided for the use of a capital reserve conversion of shares. The specific method of capital reserve Minbai Company used to convert the RMB 30 million equity assets injected by Honglou Group into shares enjoyed by all holders of tradable shares is an internal financial processing matter of Minbai Company. Although Minbai Company used the share premium portion under the capital reserve item to convert shares for all holders of tradable shares, the company's assets were not diminished in this process. Shenjun Company's claim that Minbai Company used the company's reserves to convert shares, and that Shenjun Company should therefore receive a corresponding number of shares, lacks factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it.

Shenjun Company argues on appeal that the targeted conversion of new shares from the RMB 30 million assets received by Minbai Company constituted a non-public issuance, and that this non-public issuance was not approved by the China Securities Regulatory Commission. Therefore, the content of the "Share-trading Reform Plan" passed by the shareholders' general meeting resolution regarding the conversion of RMB 30 million assets into 28,379,137 new shares is invalid. Because in its original claim, Shenjun Company sought damages from Minbai Company for 1,753,800 shares, equivalent to RMB 20,081,010, the substance of the claim was based on the premise that the shareholders' general meeting resolution and the "Share-trading Reform Plan" adopted thereby were valid. If the shareholders' general meeting resolution and the "Share-trading Reform Plan" were invalid, Shenjun Company's claims would have no basis. Furthermore, in the original trial of this case, Shenjun Company did not seek a declaration that the shareholders' general meeting resolution and the "Share-trading Reform Plan" were invalid. Its assertion of invalidity in the second instance is beyond the scope of this appeal, and this Court will not consider it. Shenjun Company's claim that Minbai Company's violation of the non-public issuance provisions of the Securities Law constitutes a criminal offense is not within the scope of this case, and this Court will not consider it.

Shenjun Company has not provided evidence that it obtained 1,753,800 shares of Minbai Company through a gratuitous donation, nor has it provided evidence that Minbai Company illegally disposed of the shares Shenjun Company obtained from that donation. Therefore, Shenjun Company's assertion that Minbai Company illegally donated the 1,753,800 new shares of Minbai Company formed by Shenjun Company's receipt of the gratuitous donation to others lacks factual basis. Shenjun Company's demand that Minbai Company compensate for damages caused by infringement has no legal basis, and this Court does not support it.

In the litigation involving Mediation Document No. 159 made by the Gansu Higher People's Court, Shenjun Company sought a declaration that the shareholders' general meeting resolution of May 29, 2006 was invalid. In the original trial of this case, Shenjun Company sought to obtain a proportionate share of shares in accordance with the "Share-trading Reform Plan" adopted by the shareholders' general meeting resolution. These are different claims. Shenjun Company's filing of the suit in the original trial of this case did not constitute re-litigation of the same matter. The original trial court's dismissal of Shenjun Company's claims based on the principle of res judicata was improper, and this Court hereby corrects it.

In conclusion, Shenjun Company's grounds of appeal lack factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support them. The facts found in the original judgment are clear, the application of law was not entirely appropriate, but the result of the judgment is correct, and this Court affirms it. Pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court hereby orders as follows:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 154,172 shall be borne by Lanzhou Shenjun Logistics Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
